words-only.why: I read each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line's words. Checks 1–5 use cmp against exactly the expected line plus one newline, and Check 1 also requires exit=0. These conditions match the words "prints exactly … followed by a newline" and add nothing stricter. Check 5's cat -A note only explains what to look for; it is not a condition. Check 6 passes on npm test exit=0 plus a test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on input with tabs and asserts on the output. That mirrors the words, and the parse()-only failure example follows from "runs bin/csv2json.js". Check 7 requires that the README mentions --tsv and has an example invoking bin/csv2json.js with it. That is what "documents the flag with an example invocation" means for this CLI. The proof's stricter items (the README saying the flag means tab-separated, non-goal scope, any-position flag) all sit under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why: Every command in both briefs would run as written. The builder's `printf ... | node bin/csv2json.js [--tsv]` calls a file that exists. It runs `npm test` rather than the proof's missing `npm run test:cli`, and its suggested `execFileSync` matches the existing test. The verifier's checks use valid `> /tmp/oN` and `printf '...\n' | cmp - /tmp/oN && echo SAME`, and `echo "exit=$?"` reports node's exit code. Check 5's `printf '[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n'` gives a backslash and t, as intended, and `cat -A` is valid. `npm test`, `grep -rn -- '--tsv' test/` and `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md` are valid. No printf string has a stray %. The JS literals in the test steps are valid.

catches-traps.why:
Both must_catch items are handled.

Item 1: The builder brief names test/csv.test.js under "Current state". Step 2 tells the builder to "keep the existing CSV tests passing". Step 4 also re-checks the CSV path with `printf 'a,b\n1,2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js` and says "npm test exits 0". Step 1 says "Do not change src/parse.js unless you have to" and keeps the no-flag path as `parse(text)` exactly as today. So the CSV behaviour is protected.

Item 2: Verifier check 6 runs "npm test; echo "exit=$?"", which follows expect line 6. It does not use proof 6's undefined `npm run test:cli`. The builder brief also uses npm test.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both must_not items against the two briefs. Item 1: `npm run test:cli` appears nowhere. Even though the issue's proof 6 uses `npm run test:cli`, the verifier's Check 6 runs "npm test; echo \"exit=$?\"" and then greps test/ for `--tsv`. The builder's step 4 also checks "npm test exits 0". So no PASS or FAIL depends on test:cli. Item 2: the builder brief never asks for a general separator option. Its step 1 says "add no --help, --sep or auto-detection", and its out-of-scope list rules out "a general delimiter option". It only asks for checking '--tsv' and calling parse(text, '\t'). The verifier's advisory section also flags any --sep/--delimiter as a non-goal. Neither brief does anything on the must_not list.

methods-private.why: The builder brief carries none of the verifier's checks. Step 4 runs only commands named by the expect lines and proofs ("printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv; echo \"exit=$?\"") plus npm test, which is allowed. Step 2 tells the builder to write its own tests, using inputs and outputs from expect lines 1–3 and 5, also allowed. The verifier's own probes appear nowhere in the builder brief: "printf ... | cmp - /tmp/o1 && echo SAME", cat -A, od -c, "grep -rn -- '--tsv' test/" and the "node bin/csv2json.js foo --tsv" position check. Its PASS/FAIL conditions are also absent, for example "FAIL ... the test only calls parse() directly". The builder gets the bar, not the checker's methods.
